# Third-party notices

<!-- Generated by tools/third-party-notices.py; do not edit by hand. Check: python3 tools/third-party-notices.py --check -->

Notices for the BlackSilk release artifacts: the binaries `blacksilk-node`, `blacksilk-miner`, `blacksilk-wallet` and `blacksilk-genesis` built by tools/release-build.sh (its default set; deploy/scripts/install-linux.sh builds the first three with it), and the Docker image of deploy/docker/Dockerfile (the first three). No CI workflow publishes binaries; `testnet-*` tags only run CI. This file is a record for redistribution, not legal advice.

**Method.** The crate set is the union, over the release targets (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`; deny.toml [graph]), of `cargo tree --locked -e normal,build --target <t> -p <the four packages>`, so features and target-specific dependencies (for example `windows-sys` on Windows, `libc` on Unix) are resolved as the release build resolves them. Build-dependencies and proc-macros are not shipped in the binaries; they are listed anyway, marked, because they are part of the build that produces them. Dev-dependencies are left out. Licence expressions are those the crates declare; copyright lines are extracted from their licence files (lines starting with "Copyright"), e-mail addresses removed; the full licence and notice texts are in §3 and §4.

**Limitations.** The list is a union: a given binary or target may not contain every crate. The copyright column is extracted mechanically; the verbatim texts in §3 and §4 are authoritative. A crate whose licence files state no copyright line shows its Cargo.toml authors instead. Copyright notices inside source files that are not repeated in a crate's licence files are not collected. Regenerate after every Cargo.lock change (the CI job `deny` runs `--check`).

## 1. BlackSilk's own code

BlackSilk's crates are licensed `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE; copyright The BlackSilk developers), except:

- `blacksilk-randomx` is a Rust port of tevador/RandomX under its `BSD-3-Clause` licence, reproduced in §4.1.
- The English word list in `blacksilk-crypto` (crypto/src/wordlist.rs) is the BIP-39 list; BIP-39 is published under the MIT licence (§4.2).

**The Rust standard library.** `std`, `core`, `alloc` and the crates the standard library vendors (for example `compiler_builtins`, `hashbrown`, `gimli`, `addr2line`) are linked into every binary, under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, copyright The Rust Project Developers (the Apache-2.0 text is in §3). The notices of the standard library's own vendored dependencies are not collected here (a limitation of this file); they are in the Rust source distribution of the toolchain used (`rust-src`, rustup component; https://github.com/rust-lang/rust).

### 4.2 BIP-39 English word list (crypto/src/wordlist.rs)

From BIP-39, "Mnemonic code for generating deterministic keys", by Marek Palatinus, Pavol Rusnak, Aaron Voisine and Sean Bowe, whose header states `License: MIT` (github.com/bitcoin/bips, bip-0039.mediawiki). BIP-39 states no copyright line; the MIT terms:

to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
